title: Long Task Decomposition
description: Learn how to decompose complex SaaS features into small, manageable tasks that AI can implement reliably without errors.
learning_objectives: Define the criteria for an 'atomic' implementation task
Create a sequential roadmap for a complex feature based on technical dependencies
Use AI as a technical architect to generate decomposition lists
Implement a verification loop to ensure each step is correct before proceeding
prerequisites: Understanding of LLM context window limitations

sections.heading: The Failure of Monolithic Prompts
sections.content_brief: Explain why asking an AI to 'build a whole feature' leads to hallucinations, omitted code (comments like // ... rest of code here), and logic errors. Contrast the monolithic approach with the decomposed approach.

sections.heading: Defining Atomic Tasks
sections.content_brief: Define 'atomic tasks' as units of work that are single-responsibility and fully testable. Provide a comparison between a 'too large' task (e.g., 'Build the billing system') and 'atomic' tasks (e.g., 'Create the Stripe webhook handler').
sections.code_context: Comparison of a monolithic prompt versus a series of atomic prompts for a specific feature.

sections.heading: Mapping Technical Dependencies
sections.content_brief: Teach the order of operations for decomposition: Database Schema -> Backend Logic/API -> Frontend Integration -> Edge Case Handling. Explain why following this sequence prevents constant refactoring.
sections.code_context: A step-by-step implementation roadmap for a 'User Subscription' feature.

sections.heading: Using AI as the Architect
sections.content_brief: Demonstrate how to use a 'Meta-Prompt' to force the AI to act as a Technical Lead. Show how to ask the AI to break down a requirement into a checklist before any code is written.
sections.code_context: A prompt template that instructs the AI to decompose a feature into a numbered list of implementation steps.

sections.heading: The Execution and Verification Loop
sections.content_brief: Describe the workflow: Execute one atomic task -> Run tests/Verify output -> Feed verification results back to AI -> Move to next task. Explain why skipping verification leads to 'error compounding'.
sections.code_context: Example of a terminal-based verification loop (running a test and pasting the error back into the AI).

admonitions.content: Avoid 'over-decomposition.' If tasks are too small (e.g., creating a single variable), the AI may lose the broader context of why the code is being written, leading to fragmented logic.
Maintain a 'Progress Log' in a separate markdown file. Paste this log into each new prompt so the AI knows exactly which steps of the decomposition are complete and what remains.
